correctness.rationale: For X=beta I+(alpha-beta)|A^(1/2)u><A^(-1/2)u|, the span of its two update vectors reduces X and X*, and X*X equals the near-spectral endpoint. Direct trace and determinant on the reducing space prove the exact two roots and flat remainder. Cauchy–Schwarz and functional calculus bound the orientation scalar, spectral endpoint approximate vectors establish sharp infima/suprema, and equality forces an equal-mass superposition of two endpoint eigenvectors. The eigenvector-degenerate case and scalar A case are explicitly handled. 8076 deterministic finite assertions were executed; they do not serve as proof.

originality.rationale: The publicly available 2026 paper defines the exact endpoint and proves its qualitative log-majorization but supplies no all-dimensional spiked two-outlier spectrum or sharp spectral-envelope/attainment theorem. Its normalized determinant-one 2-by-2 formula does not itself analyze rank-one spikes in arbitrary or infinite dimension. The 2019 rank-one perturbation literature provides general inequalities and standard rank-two principles, while Kantorovich gives only the scalar extremal factor. The complete operator spectral classification and endpoint-attainment criterion were not found in the checked records.
